enabled.doc: Enabled indicates whether to not retry sending batches in case of export failure.

initial_interval.doc: InitialInterval the time to wait after the first failure before retrying.

max_elapsed_time.doc: MaxElapsedTime is the maximum amount of time (including retries) spent trying to send a request/batch. Once this value is reached, the data is discarded. If set to 0, the retries are never stopped.

multiplier.doc: Multiplier is the value multiplied by the backoff interval bounds

randomization_factor.doc: RandomizationFactor is a random factor used to calculate next backoffs Randomized interval = RetryInterval * (1 ± RandomizationFactor)

flush_timeout.doc: FlushTimeout sets the time after which a batch will be sent regardless of its size.

max_size.doc: MaxSize defines the configuration for the maximum size of a batch.

min_size.doc: MinSize defines the configuration for the minimum size of a batch.

metadata_keys.doc: MetadataKeys is a list of client.Metadata keys that will be used to partition the data into batches. If this setting is empty, a single batcher instance will be used. partition.doc: Partition defines the partitioning of the batches configuration.

sizer.doc: Sizer determines the type of size measurement used by the batch. If not configured, use the same configuration as the queue. It accepts "requests", "items", or "bytes".

batch.doc: BatchConfig it configures how the requests are consumed from the queue and batch together during consumption.

block_on_overflow.doc: BlockOnOverflow determines the behavior when the component's TotalSize limit is reached. If true, the component will wait for space; otherwise, operations will immediately return a retryable error.

insecure_skip_verify.doc: InsecureSkipVerify will enable TLS but not verify the certificate.

cert_pem.doc: In memory PEM encoded TLS cert to use for TLS required connections. (optional)

cipher_suites.doc: CipherSuites is a list of TLS cipher suites that the TLS transport can use. If left blank, a safe default list is used. See https://go.dev/src/crypto/tls/cipher_suites.go for a list of supported cipher suites.

curve_preferences.doc: contains the elliptic curves that will be used in an ECDHE handshake, in preference order Defaults to empty list and "crypto/tls" defaults are used, internally.

include_system_ca_certs_pool.doc: If true, load system CA certificates pool in addition to the certificates configured in this struct.

insecure.doc: In gRPC and HTTP when set to true, this is used to disable the client transport security. See https://godoc.org/google.golang.org/grpc#WithInsecure for gRPC. Please refer to https://godoc.org/crypto/tls#Config for more information. (optional, default false)

insecure_skip_verify.doc: InsecureSkipVerify will enable TLS but not verify the certificate.

key_file.doc: Path to the TLS key to use for TLS required connections. (optional)

key_pem.doc: In memory PEM encoded TLS key to use for TLS required connections. (optional)

max_version.doc: MaxVersion sets the maximum TLS version that is acceptable. If not set, refer to crypto/tls for defaults. (optional)

min_version.doc: MinVersion sets the minimum TLS version that is acceptable. If not set, TLS 1.2 will be used. (optional)

reload_interval.doc: ReloadInterval specifies the duration after which the certificate will be reloaded If not set, it will never be reloaded (optional)

server_name_override.doc: ServerName requested by client for virtual hosting. This sets the ServerName in the TLSConfig. Please refer to https://godoc.org/crypto/tls#Config for more information. (optional)

path.doc: The path to the TPM device or Unix domain socket. For instance /dev/tpm0 or /dev/tpmrm0.

tls.doc: TLS struct exposes TLS client configuration.

traces_endpoint.doc: The URL to send traces to. If omitted the Endpoint + "/v1/traces" will be used.

write_buffer_size.doc: WriteBufferSize for HTTP client. See http.Transport.WriteBufferSize. Default is 0.

fields.doc: Config defines configuration for OTLP/HTTP exporter.

authenticator.doc: AuthenticatorID specifies the name of the extension to use in order to authenticate the incoming data point.

timeout.doc: Timeout is the maximum amount of time a dial will wait for a connect to complete. The default is no timeout.

dialer.doc: DialerConfig contains options for connecting to an address.

endpoint.doc: Endpoint configures the address for this network connection. For TCP and UDP networks, the address has the form "host:port". The host must be a literal IP address, or a host name that can be resolved to IP addresses. The port must be a literal port number or a service name. If the host is a literal IPv6 address it must be enclosed in square brackets, as in "[2001:db8::1]:80" or "[fe80::1%zone]:80". The zone specifies the scope of the literal IPv6 address as defined in RFC 4007.

include_metadata.doc: Include propagates the incoming connection's metadata to downstream consumers.

enforcement_policy.doc: KeepaliveEnforcementPolicy allow configuration of the keepalive.EnforcementPolicy. The same default values as keepalive.EnforcementPolicy are applicable and get applied by the server. See https://godoc.org/google.golang.org/grpc/keepalive#EnforcementPolicy for details.

server_parameters.doc: KeepaliveServerParameters allow configuration of the keepalive.ServerParameters. The same default values as keepalive.ServerParameters are applicable and get applied by the server. See https://godoc.org/google.golang.org/grpc/keepalive#ServerParameters for details.

keepalive.doc: Keepalive anchor for all the settings related to keepalive.

max_concurrent_streams.doc: MaxConcurrentStreams sets the limit on the number of concurrent streams to each ServerTransport. It has effect only for streaming RPCs.

max_recv_msg_size_mib.doc: MaxRecvMsgSizeMiB sets the maximum size (in MiB) of messages accepted by the server.

id.doc: ID specifies the name of the extension to use.

item.doc: Middleware defines the extension ID for a middleware component.

read_buffer_size.doc: ReadBufferSize for gRPC server. See grpc.ReadBufferSize. (https://godoc.org/google.golang.org/grpc#ReadBufferSize).

client_ca_file.doc: Path to the TLS cert to use by the server to verify a client certificate. (optional) This sets the ClientCAs and ClientAuth to RequireAndVerifyClientCert in the TLSConfig. Please refer to https://godoc.org/crypto/tls#Config for more information. (optional)

client_ca_file_reload.doc: Reload the ClientCAs file when it is modified (optional, default false)

path.doc: The path to the TPM device or Unix domain socket. For instance /dev/tpm0 or /dev/tpmrm0.

tls.doc: Configures the protocol to use TLS. The default value is nil, which will cause the protocol to not use TLS.

transport.doc: Transport to use. Allowed protocols are "tcp", "tcp4" (IPv4-only), "tcp6" (IPv6-only), "udp", "udp4" (IPv4-only), "udp6" (IPv6-only), "ip", "ip4" (IPv4-only), "ip6" (IPv6-only), "unix", "unixgram", "unixpacket" and "npipe" (Windows named pipes, Windows-only).

write_buffer_size.doc: WriteBufferSize for gRPC server. See grpc.WriteBufferSize. (https://godoc.org/google.golang.org/grpc#WriteBufferSize).

grpc.doc: ServerConfig defines common settings for a gRPC server configuration.

authenticator.doc: AuthenticatorID specifies the name of the extension to use in order to authenticate the incoming data point.

request_params.doc: RequestParameters is a list of parameters that should be extracted from the request and added to the context. When a parameter is found in both the query string and the header, the value from the query string will be used.

compression_algorithms.doc: CompressionAlgorithms configures the list of compression algorithms the server can accept. Default: ["", "gzip", "zstd", "zlib", "snappy", "deflate"]

allowed_headers.doc: AllowedHeaders sets what headers will be allowed in CORS requests. The Accept, Accept-Language, Content-Type, and Content-Language headers are implicitly allowed. If no headers are listed, X-Requested-With will also be accepted by default. Include "*" to allow any request header.

allowed_origins.doc: AllowedOrigins sets the allowed values of the Origin header for HTTP/JSON requests to an OTLP receiver. An origin may contain a wildcard (*) to replace 0 or more characters (e.g., "http://*.domain.com", or "*" to allow any origin).

exposed_headers.doc: ExposedHeaders sets the value of the Access-Control-Expose-Headers response header, indicating which headers are safe to expose to the API of a CORS response.

max_age.doc: MaxAge sets the value of the Access-Control-Max-Age response header. Set it to the number of seconds that browsers should cache a CORS preflight response for.

cors.doc: CORS configures the server for HTTP cross-origin resource sharing (CORS).

endpoint.doc: Endpoint configures the listening address for the server.

idle_timeout.doc: IdleTimeout is the maximum amount of time to wait for the next request when keep-alives are enabled. If IdleTimeout is zero, the value of ReadTimeout is used. If both are zero, there is no timeout.

include_metadata.doc: IncludeMetadata propagates the client metadata from the incoming requests to the downstream consumers

keep_alives_enabled.doc: KeepAlivesEnabled controls whether HTTP keep-alives are enabled. By default, keep-alives are always enabled. Only very resource-constrained environments should disable them.

logs_url_path.doc: The URL path to receive logs on. If omitted "/v1/logs" will be used.

max_request_body_size.doc: MaxRequestBodySize sets the maximum request body size in bytes. Default: 20MiB.

metrics_url_path.doc: The URL path to receive metrics on. If omitted "/v1/metrics" will be used.

id.doc: ID specifies the name of the extension to use.

item.doc: Middleware defines the extension ID for a middleware component.

middlewares.doc: Middlewares are used to add custom functionality to the HTTP server. Middleware handlers are called in the order they appear in this list, with the first middleware becoming the outermost handler.

read_header_timeout.doc: ReadHeaderTimeout is the amount of time allowed to read request headers. The connection's read deadline is reset after reading the headers and the Handler can decide what is considered too slow for the body. If ReadHeaderTimeout is zero, the value of ReadTimeout is used. If both are zero, there is no timeout.

read_timeout.doc: ReadTimeout is the maximum duration for reading the entire request, including the body. A zero or negative value means there will be no timeout. Because ReadTimeout does not let Handlers make per-request decisions on each request body's acceptable deadline or upload rate, most users will prefer to use ReadHeaderTimeout. It is valid to use them both.

value.doc: String alias that is marshaled and printed in an opaque way. To recover the original value, cast it to a string.

item.doc: Pair is an element of a MapList, and consists of a name and an opaque value.

response_headers.doc: Additional headers attached to each HTTP response sent to the client. Header values are opaque since they may be sensitive.

tls.doc: TLS struct exposes TLS client configuration.

traces_url_path.doc: The URL path to receive traces on. If omitted "/v1/traces" will be used.

write_timeout.doc: WriteTimeout is the maximum duration before timing out writes of the response. It is reset whenever a new request's header is read. Like ReadTimeout, it does not let Handlers make decisions on a per-request basis. A zero or negative value means there will be no timeout.

http.doc: ServerConfig defines settings for creating an HTTP server.

protocols.doc: Protocols is the configuration for the supported protocols, currently gRPC and HTTP (Proto and JSON).

fields.doc: Config defines configuration for OTLP receiver.
